records.reason: The actual flag has twelve white squares of area u. Its four larger blue corner triangles each have area u, and sixteen smaller blue triangles each have area u/2, so B=12u=W, source A. Independently the white-square diagonal d satisfies d²=2u; the center square has side 2d and area 8u, and the outer square has side 4d and area 32u. Subtracting white and central regions gives 32u-12u-8u=12u. Both original area routes are valid. The center is visibly dark blue or purple rather than red, but its central position identifies the separately named region R. Retain this actual display qualification without inventing a second interpretation of the clearly separated central region or withholding ordinary grading.

routes.label: Assign geoboard coordinates and compute polygon area

answerCheck.reason: Under the ordinary unit-geoboard convention the pictured boundary vertices are P=(0,5), Q=(3,4), R=(10,10), S=(4,0), with Q concave. Shoelace gives |50-95|/2=45/2, source C. A dissection proof subtracts indentation triangle PQR, area 25/2, from outer triangle PRS, area 35. Each triangle area follows from bounding rectangles and elementary right triangles. The explicit criterion of 084 is using coordinates to find simple lengths or areas; it fits the coordinate alternative but is not a universal requirement of the coordinate-free dissection alternative. Clear universal assessed 084 and retain both complete OR routes, placing 084 with shoelace only. The expected adjacent peg spacing of one is an ordinary geoboard convention and should remain a visible qualification, not a confirmed grading defect.
